title: Exact swap-equivariant pair encoder
hypothesis: A siamese encoder whose preference logit is a bias-free linear function of (h_a - h_b), with the tie logit a function of |h_a - h_b|, is exactly swap-equivariant by construction, and beats the structural baseline while approaching the sparse TF-IDF baseline after a single epoch.
changed_factor: Replace post-hoc swap averaging with architectural swap-equivariance: a shared deberta-v3-small encoder, a bias-free linear preference head on (h_a - h_b), and a non-linear tie head on |h_a - h_b|.
notes: Run on Kaggle GPU with scripts/train_symmetric_encoder.py + configs/symmetric_encoder.json, predating this project's ExperimentRun/results-runs pipeline. Provenance git commit 349c083d8c5958d4a6f777f0ce5931d4080c7a73 was DIRTY, so configs/project.json's run_policy.require_clean_git blocks registering this as a results/runs/ leaderboard entry as-is (ExperimentRun itself refuses to start a non-smoke run on a dirty tree). Results are committed as reviewable legacy-style evidence under results/baselines/symmetric_encoder/ instead (see docs/RESULTS.md). Re-run from a clean commit, ideally through make new-experiment, before treating this as leaderboard-eligible.
